feed.title: Wits AHEAD · Daily briefing
feed.subtitle: News, research, video and things to read on AI, data and human capability for higher education.
feed.rights: Wits AHEAD Research Group, Wits School of Education, University of the Witwatersrand

entry.title: Youth unemployment eases slightly to 47.3% as overall unemployment rises to 33.7% in the third quarter of 2026
entry.summary:
Di official unemployment rate climb by 0.1 percentage point to 33.7% for Q3 2026, as employment grow by 101,000 to 16.8 million, but di workforce grow pass dat. Youth unemployment (15 to 34) drop small by 0.1 percentage point to 47.3%: unemployed youth drop by 23,000 to 5.0 million, while employed youth drop by 5,000 to 5.5 million.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis na di number di group dey use for graduate pathways and just transitions. Pillar 4 dey ask whether AI dey close or open dis gap for dis same group of people.

Statistics South Africa · National statistics office

entry.title: University AI policies focus on cheating but leave data risks largely unaddressed, commentary warns
entry.summary:
One commentary for University World News talk say universities don write detailed rules against AI-assisted cheating, but dem leave small guidance on how staff and researchers fit put institution, student or research data inside AI tools. E quote one UK survey wey show say 63% of 49 higher education institutions don already adopt some AI tool, but na 37% only check risk pass dia immediate supplier, e also talk about data leak for University of Osaka wey affect 77,851 people, as reminder say di bigger risk na usually ordinary data mistake, no be di AI model itself.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, wey be responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, dis one dey remind us to check say AI governance for universities, including dis group own, dey cover data handling, no be academic integrity only.

University World News · Established higher education press (commentary)

entry.title: Wits opens a Global Higher Education Futures Centre, with a dedicated generative AI pedagogy hub
entry.summary:
University of Witwatersrand (Wits) don officially open dia Global Higher Education Futures Centre, wey dem launch for one webinar on 30 September wey over 170 teachers, institution leaders and policymakers attend. Di centre dey built around nine hubs, including one wey dey focus on generative AI teaching methods, and dem design am as answer to wetin di founders call polycrisis, na climate breakdown, geopolitical tension, generative AI disruption and inequality for Global South. Di founder, Professor Ruksana Osman, and di director, Dr Bernadette Johnson, tok say di centre go put Global South knowledge for front, instead of import ready-made models from north.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, one South African university dey build dia own framework to think about how AI dey disrupt higher education, instead of use one wey dem build somewhere else, and dis na exactly di Global South-led, equity-centred approach wey Wits AHEAD dey support.

University of the Witwatersrand · University announcement

entry.title: Wording of university generative AI policies shapes how students and teachers actually behave, study finds
entry.summary:
Some researchers check di generative AI policies from 101 universities for United States, dem also tok to 20 students and 20 lecturers to sabi how di rules dey work for real life. Dem find out say di exact wording of a rule, no be just wetin di rule talk, fit change how students behave: rule wey dem build around dishonesty make students hide dia AI use because of fear, while rule wey dem build around accountability encourage dem to dey open about am. Di lecturers sef tok say dem get extra approval work for hand, and dem no get reliable way to check if students dey comply.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 1, dis study remind us say generative AI policy no fit better pass how dem word am: universities wey dey write or change dia own rules on AI for teaching and assessment need to test no be only wetin di rule allow, but how students and staff go read and act on di words demsef.

arXiv preprint (University of Maryland and University of Iowa researchers) · Preprint (not yet peer-reviewed)

entry.title: How deeply students engage with an AI chat, not how often they use it, predicts better coursework, large Australian study finds
entry.summary:
Researchers for University of Queensland and Monash University study 1,681 students across 40 university courses wey dey use AI companion wey dem build inside resource creation, peer moderation and practice work. Dem code 829 conversation threads to check cognitive engagement, dem also model almost 3,000 task sequences, dem find out say students wey engage AI well-well, no be just students wey dey chat with am plenty-plenty, na dem produce better final work, no matter how many message dem exchange. After one wrong attempt, students wey talk to AI try less, but dem dey correct well-well when dem try again.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 2, dis finding important for any institution wey dey build analytics around AI tool use: to just count how many time students open chatbot no tell you anything serious about learning, so systems wey suppose support student success need to check how deep di engagement be, no be how many time dem click.

University of Queensland and Monash University (arXiv preprint, submitted to the Journal of Computer Assisted Learning) · Working paper (arXiv preprint, submitted to the Journal of Computer Assisted Learning)

entry.title: Grade the process, not just the AI-era output, Bristol pro vice-chancellor tells student success conference
entry.summary:
For one Student Success UK and Ireland conference wey Times Higher Education organise, Tansy Jessop, wey be pro vice-chancellor for education and students for University of Bristol, tok say universities don pass di stage wia dem just dey police how students use generative AI well-well, dem need to design assessment wey go show how student reach im answer instead. She explain one computer science case for Bristol, where robot-design work dem submit na pure AI-generated most times, and dis make staff to just give students one complete robot, make dem find out how dem build am. Jessop tok say dis approach go help students develop skills wey AI no fit easily replace, like curiosity, critical thinking and collaboration.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 1, dis one give real, classroom-level answer to di assessment integrity question: instead of dey chase unreliable AI detectors, make dem build tasks wey go show how student dey think, and make human still dey di one wey judge.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: AI-generated 'slop' papers published under prominent academics' names without their consent
entry.summary:
Some journals wey resemble each other dey publish papers wey AI generate, dem put am for name of popular academics, including Jure Leskovec and Fei-Fei Li from Stanford, wey talk say dem never write or submit di work at all. Times Higher Education report say one paper come back again under different author name few days after dem flag am and remove am, and di journals dey share di same editor-in-chief and board members wey no even know say dem dey list dem. Di three journals, wey dem register for 2026 only, dey charge authors between ten and two hundred US dollars for each paper.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, dis one show how generative AI fit use create not just research findings, but researchers' own identity too, na why responsible AI policy for higher education must reach publishing integrity, no be only classroom.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: Staff overestimate how much students use generative AI, Manchester study finds
entry.summary:
One study wey dem do for one social science school for one university for United Kingdom show say university staff dey over-estimate how often students dey use generative AI for their study. Based on questions wey dem ask 45 staff and 86 students for University of Manchester, staff rate students' AI use as 5.23 for scale of seven, well pass students own average wey be 3.11. Students too show say dem happy pass staff about how AI fit help productivity and learning, dem talk say dem dey use am mostly to find answer, write work and fix grammar.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 1, di gap between wetin staff think and wetin students really dey do show why policy on generative AI and how dem dey design teaching need to stand on evidence wey come from students demsef, no be staff own assumption, as universities for Global South too dey think about similar assumption.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Habit, not enjoyment, drives ChatGPT use among distance students at the University of South Africa, study of 294 finds
entry.summary:
One study of 294 students for University of South Africa, di biggest distance education institution for Africa, use di UTAUT2 model check why students dey use ChatGPT. Habit na di strongest thing wey predict both di plan to use ChatGPT and di real use, then facilitating conditions like guidance and resources follow, but enjoyment and wetin friends think no make any serious difference. Di model explain 69.2% of di students' plan to use di tool and 37.9% of how dem really use am.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 1, di finding say habit and support from di institution, no be say di thing new, na im dey drive use, show say universities suppose shape how students dey use AI every day through guidance and course design, especially for distance learning for di Global South.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Africa and Europe seek their own path on AI in science, with shared computing and genomic data on the agenda
entry.summary:
For one African Union and European Union meeting on AI for science on 26 October, wey dem do online instead of for Addis Ababa as dem plan, European Commission official Maria Cristina Russo talk say United States and China don move very far ahead and say Europe and Africa need dia own way. Speakers call for shared regional computing, one continent-wide framework for genomic data and benefit sharing, and targets wey dem fit measure for women, wey be about one-fifth of di world data and AI workforce. Di recommendations go reach AU-EU research and innovation ministers meeting wey dem shift go 2027, University World News report.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, dis meeting put data ownership, fair access to computing power and movement of talent for di centre of AI policy, questions wey go decide weda African universities go shape AI for research or dem go just dey use am.

University World News · Established higher education press

entry.title: UNESCO: university enrolment in the Arab States has nearly tripled to almost 15 million, yet youth unemployment stands at 26%
entry.summary:
New UNESCO report, The state of higher education in the Arab States, find say di number of university students for di region don almost triple inside 25 years, reach almost 15 million students, but di enrolment rate, wey be 37% for 2024, still dey below di world average of 44%. Women now be almost half of di STEM graduates for di region, compare to just over one-third for di whole world, but youth unemployment don reach 26%, almost double di world average. Dem launch di report for Doha on 4 November, e get ten recommendations, and e note say more than 70% of Arab States don put digital goals inside dia national higher education plan.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 5, dis one show wetin regional higher education data fit reveal: plenty access no mean much if di system no dey check weda graduates dey find work, di same test wey South Africa and di whole Global South dey face.

UNESCO (IESALC and UNESCO Office Beirut) · Intergovernmental body report

entry.title: Deep Learning Indaba video: Vukosi Marivate on governing AI in Africa and what a degree is worth now
entry.summary:
For one 36-minute interview wey dem record during Deep Learning Indaba 2026 for Pan-Atlantic University for Lagos, Professor Vukosi Marivate, wey co-found di Indaba, Masakhane NLP and Lelapa AI, and one of di 40 experts for di United Nations Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, explain wetin e mean to advise government on AI and why to govern AI for South Africa touch every ministry. E talk say sovereignty mean power to take action, no be to build everything for house, say AI no break assessment but e expose am, and say Africa suppose move from brain drain go brain circulation.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 4, im questions about wetin degree worth for dis AI time, and weda Africa dey train cheap AI labour for export, touch di heart of graduate capability and just transitions for di Global South.

Deep Learning Indaba (YouTube) · Africa's machine learning community, official video channel

entry.title: South Korea vows to prosecute students using AI glasses in exams
entry.summary:
South Korea Ministry of Education talk say from next year, dem go treat cheating for national university entrance exam wit AI smart glasses as criminal matter, after dem catch three students wey wear di device during essay exam for Seoul universities. From 2027, anybody dem catch go face three-year ban from di exam, instead of one year now, and inspectors go dey all di 1,312 exam centre to watch suspicious glasses.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na clear sign of how fast generative AI tools dey overtake exam integrity rule worldwide (Pillar 1), and reminder say detection and punishment na only part of di answer wey universities and system go need.

Times Higher Education · Established press

entry.title: AI Article Reviews Dominate Human Peer Reviews at Their Best: Evidence and Policy Choices
entry.summary:
Gary King and Steven Worthington wey dey Harvard Institute for Quantitative Social Science compare peer review wey AI write wit 134 human review for 124 manuscript wey dem collect between 2019 and 2026. Dem report say di review wey Claude Opus 4.8 generate pass di human review for every measure wey dem build, dem judge am to be more accurate for dia own check, and three former journal editor prefer am for most of di head-to-head comparison.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na serious, data-based challenge for how dem dey use generative AI for academic work, no be only for classroom (Pillar 1): if AI fit review research well, universities and journals need policy for when and how to use am, no be just whether to ban am.

Institute for Quantitative Social Science, Harvard University · University working paper

entry.title: Proposal 14: Student outcomes indicators
entry.summary:
England higher education regulator, Office for Students, don propose to change di one single pass-or-fail level wey dem dey use measure graduate progression to three measures wey dem go compare for dia Teaching Excellence Framework: continuing progression to work or more school, how graduates salary compare to national benchmark, and whether graduates talk say dem dey use wetin dem learn, based on Graduate Outcomes survey. Dem go adjust dis measures based on course, location, entry qualification, and students socio-economic background, instead of dey use one fixed national level for all course.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na real test for Pillar 5 main question: whether data system wey dem build from plenty benchmark measures, instead of one hard national level, fit judge higher education outcomes well well and improve dem.

Office for Students (OfS) · National regulator consultation

entry.title: UCT engineering pairs AI-enabled early warning with a multilingual support hub to lift student success
entry.summary:
Researchers for University of Cape Town Faculty of Engineering and the Built Environment dey describe a Student Success Project wey combine early risk-assessment framework, mentorship wey senior students dey lead, and one data-driven, AI-enabled support hub. Dis hub come wit multilingual digital glossary for isiXhosa, Sesotho, Kiswahili and Afrikaans, wey dey address language marginalisation alongside academic risk. Di chapter dey appear inside Constellations of Hope, one Club of Rome report on transformative learning.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na correct, verified South African example of predictive analytics for student success (pillar two) wey dem build around multilingual fairness, e dey show say early warning data go only help students if di support wey follow am still dey speak dia language.

Globethics Publications (Club of Rome report) · Peer-reviewed book chapter

entry.title: AI literacy alone does not create graduate opportunity, Nigerian study of 450 students finds; technology readiness is what matters
entry.summary:
One survey of 450 Nigerian university students show say both entrepreneurship education and AI literacy dey raise students' technology readiness, and say na dis readiness sabi predict whether dem go turn AI tools into real micro-entrepreneurial business. Wen students feel say resource dey scarce, e dey weaken dia entrepreneurial action directly, but e dey strengthen di link between readiness and action once students don get di tools.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na direct evidence for pillar four: access to AI alone no fit create opportunity for graduates wey dey tight-resource settings; na capability-building and technology readiness dey turn AI literacy into real human capability and livelihood.

Journal of Entrepreneurship in Emerging Economies · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Computational text indicators fail to improve, and can worsen, predictions of academic results, Salvadoran study warns
entry.summary:
Researchers for Universidad Salvadoreña Alberto Masferrer test whether machine-learning text indicators of students' epistemic norms fit improve prediction of academic results pass simple household and resource data. Among 263 students wey dem observe for two waves for five sites, di computer indicators no add any reliable predictive value, and one version even make prediction significantly worse after dem correct for multiple comparisons.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Na clear warning for pillar five: AI-derived text or behaviour proxy no suppose dey treated as fit for high-stakes education decisions without strong testing, na discipline wey Wits AHEAD dey apply for dia own analytics work.

Journal of Applied Research in Higher Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: LMS activity, pacing and attendance are the strongest predictors of retention in blended courses, Turkish study finds
entry.summary:
One study for Journal of Higher Education Policy and Management, wey İrfan Ayhan of Kırşehir Ahi Evran University for Türkiye write, check how predictive analytics wey dem take from learning-management-system activity, pace, assessment behaviour and attendance fit show students wey dey for risk for blended higher education courses. E find out say dis signs na di strongest tins wey fit predict retention, and e argue say, if dem use am well, predictive analytics fit strengthen early-warning systems and guide institution strategy, as far as institutions dey also think about di ethics of how dem dey use dat kain data.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about AI and predictive analytics for student success, dis study remind us say di data wey already dey sidon for most universities' learning-management systems, no be only new AI tools, fit power one early-warning system wey dey work well if dem combine am with clear ethical framework.

Journal of Higher Education Policy and Management · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Short hands-on workshop lifts science teachers' confidence in using AI for adaptive teaching, German pilot study finds
entry.summary:
One pilot study wey dem publish for Frontiers in Education, wey Mathea Brückner, Christoph Thyssen and Johannes Huwer, from di universities of Konstanz, Pädagogische Hochschule Thurgau and Pädagogische Hochschule Freiburg do, test whether one short, hands-on workshop fit raise lower-secondary science teachers' confidence for how dem dey use AI do adaptive teaching. For one before-and-after study wey involve 16 multiplier teachers for Germany, both teachers' feeling say AI dey useful and dia own confidence wey dem report demsef, rise well-well after di workshop, and di two tins only come dey strongly connect after dat time. Di authors warn say dis small sample, wey dem self report, show change, but e no prove say di workshop na im cause lasting improvement.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar wey dey about AI and analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis study show one practical, cheap format, short hands-on workshop, wey teacher-training programmes fit test and adapt to build science teachers' confidence for AI tools.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: World Bank video: 'small AI', not big models alone, can widen opportunity in developing-economy education and jobs
entry.summary:
For di Global AI and Digital Summit wey happen for Seoul, wey World Bank Group record, dia President, Ajay Banga, open one panel discussion about how "small AI", wey be practical tools wey fit local condition, no be only big general model, fit increase opportunity for developing economy. Nigeria Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Bosun Tijani, join Tridge CEO Hoshik Shin and Amini founder Kate Kallot discuss education, farming and public service, including one part wey talk about lesson wey dem learn from how dem dey use AI for education for El Salvador. Di panel talk say reliable local data, affordable connection, computing power, skill and procurement system na di conditions wey go make local innovators fit scale dia AI solutions.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about AI, graduate capability, employability and just transition, dis discussion show say AI promise dey depend on practical conditions, skill, infrastructure and procurement, wey go decide whether developing economy universities and system go really benefit, no be only dia mate for Global North wey get more resources.

World Bank Group (YouTube) · International financial institution, official video channel

entry.title: Review of generative AI ethics in higher education finds Africa only 11% of the evidence, calls for Ubuntu-informed governance
entry.summary:
One systematic review wey dem publish for Education Sciences journal, by Pearl Yarkor Yarboi and im colleague dem for University of Ghana, check 246 studies wey dem publish between 2018 and 2025 about ethics of generative AI for higher education, and dem find out say African institution dey only make up around 11.4 percent of di studies, and Ghana institution na only 2.8 percent. Dem group di wahala wey dey repeat into five area, academic integrity, privacy and data security, transparency and accountability, equity and access, and AI literacy, and dem talk say Ghana institution especially no get strong systematic governance.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about AI wey get responsibility, ethics, equity and policy, dis review wey dey call for ethical framework wey fit African context and wey dey use Ubuntu spirit, no be di one wey dem import from Global North, dey connect well well with how di group dey approach generative AI for African higher education.

Education Sciences · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Systematic review of 50 studies finds university AI governance works best when oversight, integrity rules and data risk are managed together
entry.summary:
One systematic review wey dem publish for Frontiers in Education journal, wey Fritz D. Bacalso and im colleague dem for Cebu Technological University for Philippines lead, check 221 records based on PRISMA 2020 protocol and bring togeda 50 studies about how higher education institution dey govern generative AI. Dem find out say effective adoption dey depend on governance maturity: how di university units dey work togeda well, clear academic integrity and disclosure rules, and data governance wey base for risk, plus efficiency and learning gain wen pedagogical support dey follow di technology. Di review also show big gap between regions, dem talk about one study wey show say universities six for South Africa don get formal AI policy, but none of di institution dem sample for Ghana or Nigeria get governance framework wey public fit see.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about generative AI for teaching, assessment and integrity, dis evidence wey show say governance maturity, no be only access to tools, na wetin dey decide outcome, dey support di idea say African universities need build governance wey work togeda well, no be policy wey dey only for paper.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Systematic review proposes a two-part framework for generative AI and academic integrity in higher education
entry.summary:
One systematic literature review wey dem publish for di journal AI and Ethics, wey Batool Hendal and Gobinda Chowdhury write, check 274 coded findings from research wey already dey about generative AI for higher education, and dem group dem into six themes, including di benefits and risks, how AI text detectors no dey reliable well well, and institution policy and governance. Based on dis evidence, di authors propose Academic GenAI Adaptation Framework, wey stand on two pillars, governance and infrastructure for one side, education and literacy for di oda side, as practical way wey universities fit use adopt generative AI responsibly instead of just dey police am.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about generative AI for teaching, assessment and integrity, dis framework give African universities one structured way wey different from policing wey base on detection, wey dem build from evidence wey dem don gather, no be from one institution experience.

AI and Ethics · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Mixed-methods study of 1,685 publications and 48 interviews finds generative AI is reshaping assessment, not just fuelling misconduct
entry.summary:
One mixed-methods study wey dem publish for journal SN Social Sciences, wey Florieza M. Mangubat and Fernando N. Mangubat write, join bibliometric analysis of 1,685 Scopus-indexed publications about academic integrity and assessment wit interview of 48 students and lecturers for higher education institutions for Cebu region, Philippines. Dem find say scholarly attention to di topic rise well-well after 2022, say students dey use generative AI for learning and academic work but dem no too sure wetin be acceptable use, and say lecturers dey respond by redesigning assessment make e focus on authentic, process-based tasks instead of to rely only on AI-detection tools.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about generative AI for teaching, assessment and integrity, how institutions for anoda part of Global South dey move from policing go redesigning assessment match wetin African universities already dey consider, and e strengthen di idea say to reform assessment better pass to depend on detection.

SN Social Sciences · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Systematic review of 463 studies finds AI in Global South universities still mostly administrative, not pedagogical
entry.summary:
One systematic review and bibliometric analysis wey dem publish for journal Frontiers in Education, wey Nomfundo Gladys Khoza and Freda van der Walt, from Central University of Technology, Free State, South Africa write, check articles 947 and include 463 peer-reviewed studies, wey dem publish between 2019 and 2025, about AI teaching methods for higher education for Global South. Dem find say most AI use still dey aim for technical efficiency and admin work, say real teaching integration still small, and say weak infrastructure, unequal access to digital tools, poor teacher readiness and ethical worry be di main barriers, while solutions wey fit local area and collaborative innovation be di clearest opportunity.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work wey dey about generative AI for teaching and about responsible, fair AI policy, how dem find say admin use still pass real teaching innovation across Global South na reminder say African universities, including Wits, need to invest on purpose for teacher readiness and teaching method wey fit local area, no be just access to AI tools.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article (systematic review)

entry.title: US universities race to launch AI majors as the count passes 100, nearly double in a year
entry.summary:
More than 100 universities for America don now offer undergraduate degree for artificial intelligence inside computer science department, wey almost double di number from one year ago, according to database wey Northeastern University Center for Inclusive Computing dey keep. Bentley University AI degree don grow from small-small students wen dem launch am for 2024 to almost 100 students dis year, while MIT AI and Decision Making degree, wey start for 2022, be di second most popular course for di university now, wit 354 students wey register. School management say dis rush connect to how students dey worry about job market wey AI don change, and how employers dey look for graduates wey sabi AI; one study wey dem do for May show say just small pass one-third of 66 schools wey dem survey, wey offer AI degree, dey require ethics course.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work on AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, how big and how fast dis change dey happen for Global North, plus di uneven way ethics training dey required, be one marker wey Wits AHEAD fit use to think how African universities suppose design similar AI qualifications wit responsibility, no just as reaction.

WBUR · Public radio news report

entry.title: Study combines AI-TPACK and Freire's critical pedagogy to rethink AI in African STEM curricula
entry.summary:
Two researchers for University of South Africa (UNISA) come up with one framework wey go help bring artificial intelligence (AI) enter STEM subjects (science, technology, engineering and maths) across Africa, as dem combine AI-TPACK model with Paulo Freire critical pedagogy. Dem base di paper on review of wetin oda people don write, no field work, and dem look tools like intelligent tutoring systems, adaptive learning platforms and automatic marking, dem talk say dis fit reduce wahala for classrooms wey too full and no get enough resources. Di paper recommend strategies wey fit di local culture and ethics, wey go address infrastructure gap, teacher capacity and di way-way different situations, so dat AI no go make inequality worse pass wetin dey now.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work on AI and data analytics for STEM and teacher education, dis paper give one critical framework wey dey rooted for Africa, to weigh AI promise for STEM teaching against di real wahala of infrastructure and teacher capacity for di continent, na warning wey suppose slow down any rush to adopt AI.

Eurasia Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education (University of South Africa) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Survey finds most Built Environment students use AI chatbots but African universities still lack formal AI policy
entry.summary:
One survey of Built Environment students, wey dem present for FIG Congress 2026 for Cape Town, show say 74 percent of dem don already dey use AI chatbot for school work, and dem get mostly positive mind about am, but dem talk say dem no get enough guidance from dia school. Di writers, wey dey write from Namibia and Nigeria, talk say na only small-small universities for South Africa, including Wits, University of Cape Town, University of Pretoria and University of Johannesburg, don develop AI guidelines since 2024, while almost 70 percent of universities for America don already get written AI policy. Dem give roadmap for how African universities fit build AI governance wey fit dia own situation.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD pillar on responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, di fact say plenty African schools still no get formal AI policy, even as students dey use AI chatbot everywhere, show how governance dey lag behind practice; di roadmap wey di paper give fit be good starting point to close dat gap.

FIG Congress 2026 (International Federation of Surveyors), Cape Town · Conference paper (International Federation of Surveyors)

entry.title: WISE and Education Collaborative partner with five African universities on an AI adoption pilot
entry.summary:
WISE (World Innovation Summit for Education) and Ashesi University Education Collaborative don start AI pilot project with five African universities: Bells University of Technology for Nigeria, Botho University for Botswana, KCA University for Kenya, University of Kigali for Rwanda, and Université d'Abomey-Calavi for Benin. From October 2026 reach June 2027, each university go test one project wey fit its own priority, from AI tutors wey match curriculum and adaptive learning tools, to early-warning systems and institutional governance frameworks. The pilot dey build on top one 2025 baseline study of 47 African universities, wey show say AI adoption no dey balance and governance still weak.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD work on responsible AI governance, na rare multi-country trial wey dey test AI tools and institutional policy together across five African universities wey different well well, and e dey give early comparative evidence of wetin responsible AI adoption fit be for real life.

africa.com (WISE and The Education Collaborative, Ashesi University) · International education initiative announcement

entry.title: Early success indicators at a South African university: a data-centric approach to student success
entry.summary:
Philokuhle Majozi and Kgadi Mathabathe, wey dey University of Pretoria, don bring one new framework wey dem call "early success indicators." Di framework dey track data and support wey students go need from before dem register reach di final exam. Dem base di work on interview wey dem do wit academic success coaches, school leaders and data scientists, and di framework dey focus on wetin students dey good for, instead of di old "at risk" early warning system wey dey show wahala.

Why e matter for AHEAD: Dis one give Wits AHEAD predictive analytics work one South African, strength based option wey different from di normal early warning model, and e fit helep dem design support wey go helep students wey dey struggle, no be just to mark dem.

Journal of Student Affairs in Africa · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Cambridge-led OpRaise report: AI markers favour style over substance in university essays
entry.summary:
Researchers from University of Cambridge, Manchester Metropolitan and Nottingham test three top AI models, one by one and togeda, on 761 undergraduate psychology essay from three UK universities. Di models agree well among demsef, but dem no agree well well with human markers, as dem dey always favour long, complex writing no matter di quality, and dem dey push marks go di middle of di scale.

Why e matter for AHEAD: As Wits AHEAD dey think how AI fit work for assessment, dis strong research wey cover many institutions show say automatic marking still dey favour style pass substance, na warning for Global South universities, wey get bigger class and fewer markers, no to replace human judgement with AI.

University of Cambridge, Manchester Metropolitan University and the University of Nottingham (OpRaise project) · University research report

entry.title: World Bank video: Korea Partnership Facility forum explores AI for education and skills
entry.summary:
YouTube channel of World Bank Group don release one short video about dis year Korea-World Bank Group Partnership Facility forum, where officials from Korea Ministry of Economy and Finance, World Bank specialists, and one KAIST professor talk how AI fit strengthen learning and prepare people for future work. Di Facility dey fund AI and digital skills programmes for education and work systems for developing countries.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 4, dis one show say international financial institutions dey now see AI skills training as something wey central to graduate employability and just transitions, no be extra ting.

World Bank Group (YouTube) · International financial institution, official video channel

entry.title: Study finds South African universities' AI policies strong on student rules, thin on privacy and staff duties
entry.summary:
One study wey check di generative AI guidelines wey South Africa public universities don publish show say na 46 per cent of di institutions get institution-wide policy wen dem do di research. Where guidelines dey, dem set clear rules for transparency and student accountability, but dem only talk about privacy, data governance and staff accountability small-small, mostly as advice no be binding rule.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 6, dis one be direct evidence for Wits AHEAD: di authors dey call for harmonised AI guidance wey dem design from scratch to protect privacy, na exactly di responsible AI gap wey di group dey track.

Universal Access in the Information Society · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Smartphone AI tools help STEM teachers in low-resource African classrooms move beyond chalk and talk, study finds
entry.summary:
One case study wey Universiti Sains Malaysia lead work with ten STEM teachers from Nigeria, Botswana, Ghana, Namibia and Sierra Leone for one hands-on workshop wey use AI tools wey turn voice to picture, block coding for phone, and circuit simulation. Di teachers talk say di tools make hard science ideas easy to show, make students wey no get laptop fit learn coding skills for phone, and make dem fit test circuit safely before dem touch real equipment wey scarce.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Pillar 3, dis one be good evidence say well-chosen, cheap AI tools, no be expensive equipment, be wetin fit change STEM teaching for African classroom wey no get enough resources, from chalk and talk to real inquiry.

ECNU Review of Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Africa must build its own AI and data, not just adopt it, UFS tells QS Africa Forum
entry.summary:
For di QS Africa Forum 2026 wey happen for Addis Ababa, Professor Sam Tshehla, Deputy Vice Chancellor for University of the Free State (UFS), talk for di session about AI imperative and di future of higher education sey African universities must stop to just dey react to AI, make dem build dia own data and systems wey show Africa language, culture and development wahala. E talk sey AI fit help from admission reach teaching and research, but na only if dem invest well-well for digital literacy, governance and ethical rules.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 6 work on AI wey dey responsible, ethics, fairness and policy, dis call for Africa to own dia data and systems match wetin Wits AHEAD dey always talk about, say AI governance for Global South suppose come from inside, no be import from outside.

University of the Free State · University report

entry.title: AI exposure linked to 13 percentage point rise in top grades, Berkeley working paper finds
entry.summary:
One working paper by Igor Chirikov of Center for Studies in Higher Education for University of California, Berkeley, check more than 500,000 grades wey dem give from 2018 to 2025 for one big research university. For classes wey get plenty writing and coding work, di A grades increase by 13 percentage points after ChatGPT come out, na like 30 percent pass wetin dey happen for 2022. Di increase big well-well where take-home work dey count more for final grade.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 1 work on generative AI for teaching, assessment and integrity, dis study na warning sey higher grades no always mean better learning: di work wey Wits AHEAD dey do to change how dem dey assess student need consider dis same risk for take-home work.

Center for Studies in Higher Education, UC Berkeley · Working paper, University of California, Berkeley (CSHE)

entry.title: Generative AI closes three-quarters of the productivity gap between more and less educated workers, NBER study finds
entry.summary:
One working paper from National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), wey Guillermo Cruces, Diego Fernández Meijide, Sebastian Galiani, Ramiro H. Gálvez and María Lombardi write, show one experiment wey dem do with 1,174 adults wey do business problem-solving task. Without generative AI, people wey get higher education dey perform pass people wey get lower education with 0.548 standard deviation; but with AI help, di gap drop to 0.139 standard deviation, wey close almost three-quarter of di first gap. Di advantage no stay well-well sotey dem comot di AI tool for one task wey follow.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 4 work on human capability, employability and just transitions, dis finding fit two ways: generative AI fit shrink long-time gap for how people dey perform, but di advantage go fade if no dey try well-well, so di way wey dem dey teach students still need build di real capability wey AI just dey support.

National Bureau of Economic Research · Working paper, National Bureau of Economic Research

entry.title: World Bank warns AI's benefits in Africa could bypass the poorest households
entry.summary:
World Bank Africa Economic Update for October 2026, wey dem call 'Building AI Readiness', dey predict say Sub-Saharan Africa economy go grow from 4.1 percent for 2025 reach 4.3 percent for 2026, as developer activity dey rise fast: Nigeria software developer community for GitHub don grow ten times since 2020, and Ghana own don grow almost eight times. Di report talk say AI fit increase productivity and create work for di region, but e say how pipo dey use AI still no balance, e dey concentrate for just few economy, especially Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa. E mention steady light, affordable internet, digital skills and government capacity as tins wey still dey missing for most part of di region.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 6 work on AI wey dey responsible, fairness and policy, dis report na clear warning: higher education systems for Global South no fit assume say AI benefit go just come by itself; to build basic digital and institutional capacity still remain di important first step.

World Bank · Intergovernmental regional economic report

entry.title: Critical review finds Ghana's national AI strategy strong on readiness but thin on classroom detail
entry.summary:
One critical policy analysis wey Matthew Nyaaba and nine oda co-author write, build one Education-Centred AI Policy Framework, dem use am check Ghana National Artificial Intelligence Strategy for 2025 to 2035. Di paper see say di strategy dey strong well-well for AI literacy, youth skills and workforce readiness, but e never develop well for teacher agency, teacher training before dem start work, curriculum and assessment guide, how to teach pipo wey speak different language and culture, and how community fit dey part of decision for school level. Di authors talk say Ghana need one plan wey focus on education wey go connect workforce goal to teacher training, curriculum change and protection for learners.

Why e matter for AHEAD: For Wits AHEAD Pillar 6 work on AI wey dey responsible, ethics, fairness and policy, dis analysis dey useful reminder say national AI strategy for Global South dey often run ahead of di real wahala wey dey classroom, wey must happen first before di strategy fit work well for teacher and student.
